title: Select vs Include
description: Optimize query payloads by understanding the fundamental difference between select and include in Prisma Client.

data.text: In Prisma, controlling the shape of returned data is accomplished via `select` and `include`. Understanding how they differ and when to use each is crucial for writing efficient queries that minimize network payload size and memory footprint.

data.title: How They Work
items: **`select`**: Explicitly chooses which scalar and relational fields to return. Any field not listed is excluded from the query (`SELECT id, email FROM ...`).
**`include`**: Returns **ALL** default scalar fields on the model, plus adds specified relational models (`SELECT * FROM users` plus relation join).

data.title: Mutually Exclusive at the Root Level
data.text: You cannot use `select` and `include` simultaneously on the same level of a query! If you want to include relations while selecting only specific parent fields, nest `select` inside `select`.

data.title: Wrong vs Right: Mixing Select and Include
data.content: How to properly select specific parent fields while loading related records.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Prefer `select` in production APIs to prevent leaking sensitive fields like password hashes.
Use `include` when you need all scalar fields of an entity plus related entities.
Never mix `select` and `include` at the same object depth.
